newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia facing budget shortfall, tough year.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia facing budget shortfall, tough year.

text.p: Finance Minister Keat Chhon said on Monday Cambodia was facing a tough budget shortfall but expressed hopes that new tax measures and forestry income would boost government revenue in 1997.

Speaking at a meeting with top foreign aid officials and diplomats, Keat Chhon said lower than expected revenues for January-March had caused the government to spend only 55 percent of budgeted expenditures.

"In the first quarter of 1997, current expenditures were maintained to the strict minimum of about 119.3 billion riels ($43.6 million), which is 45 percent less than programmed. This we did to maintain our commitments for financial stability," he said.
The bulk of the austerity measures fell on the operational costs for civil administration, Keat Chhon said.
The cutbacks were forced by an 18 percent drop in customs revenues and a 15 percent drop in turnover taxes, he said, without explaining the reason for the falls.
"However, we still believe that budget revenues will improve during the year, given the fact that some of the tax measures (of the 1997 tax law) have not come into effect," Keat Chhon said.
He added that $2 million in forestry revenues for the first quarter were still trickling into the national treasury.
International donors have criticised the government for allowing generous tax exemptions for garment and forestry exporters, which analysts said may have prompted the decline in revenues.
Keat Chhon has said the 1997 tax law, which has yet to take effect, will close some loopholes and broaden the country's tiny tax base.
